metadata.scope: Roof trusses, bridge trusses, king-post, queen-post, Pratt, Howe, Warren, Fink, and K-truss layouts with features, parameters, formulas, assumptions, and OpenSCAD generation patterns.

material_suggestions.use_case: welded or bolted bridge, roof, and plant trusses
material_suggestions.notes: Good default for load-bearing steel trusses; compression members still require buckling checks.

material_suggestions.use_case: clean welded trusses, machine frames, crane booms, and gantries
material_suggestions.notes: Better torsional stiffness than flat bar for 3D frames.

material_suggestions.use_case: king-post, queen-post, Fink, and architectural roof trusses
material_suggestions.notes: Use larger member depths and bolted or toothed connector plates.

material_suggestions.use_case: lightweight removable display rigs and non-permanent frames
material_suggestions.notes: Lower stiffness than steel; increase section depth and control member slenderness.
Do not treat printed polymer trusses as certified structural parts.

standards_used.name: General truss design practice
standards_used.applies_to: member layout, panel points, and node-to-node modeling
standards_used.note: Members should meet at common nodes; panel_length = span / panel_count.

standards_used.name: AISC / Eurocode steel design principles
standards_used.note: Compression members require buckling checks; tension members require net-section and connection checks.

standards_used.name: Timber truss detailing practice
standards_used.applies_to: king-post, queen-post, and Fink roof trusses
standards_used.note: Timber trusses typically use larger sections and connector plates.

output_policy.openscad_code: Geometry-only OpenSCAD with named parameters, one module, and no prose.

parts.name: Common truss features, parameters, formulas, and assumptions

main_parameters.rise: roof-truss height from bottom chord to apex
main_parameters.depth: bridge-truss distance between top and bottom chord centerlines
main_parameters.panel_count: number of repeated bays along the span
main_parameters.truss_type: king_post, queen_post, pratt, howe, warren, fink, or k_truss
main_parameters.truss_width: overall side spacing or plate direction

non_main_parameters.gusset_radius: node plate radius or visual half-width
non_main_parameters.bolt_diameter: bolt or hole diameter at gussets
non_main_parameters.edge_distance: minimum bolt center to plate edge
non_main_parameters.member_clearance: small clearance between overlapping visual members
non_main_parameters.side_spacing: distance between paired side trusses in a 3D bridge

rafter_length.note: king-post or simple pitched rafter length

depth_default.note: visual default for simple bridge trusses

assumptions: Geometry is conceptual CAD, not certified structural analysis.
Members are straight, prismatic, and joined at common endpoint nodes.
Loads are assumed to enter at panel points for truss-style force paths.
Compression members require buckling checks outside OpenSCAD.
Tension members require net-section and connection checks outside OpenSCAD.
main_features: web members made from diagonals and verticals
support pads or bearing plates at both ends
design_rules: Use endpoint-based member_between(p1,p2) placement for every chord and web.
Do not model a truss as one filled triangular plate.
Keep span, rise or depth, panel_count, member size, gusset size, and bolt diameter as named parameters.
Place gusset plates at nodes where members meet.
Use support pads at left and right bearing points when realistic detail is requested.
validation_criteria: separate visible members between node points
support pads at left and right supports
failure_modes: single solid triangle instead of a member assembly
web members do not meet at common nodes
no gusset plates on a realistic bolted truss

parts.name: King-post roof truss

main_parameters.rise: height from tie beam to apex

strut_node_z.formula: rise / 2 for midpoint nodes on straight rafters

assumptions: Short roof span with one central post.
The bottom chord acts as a tie between supports.
Struts run from the bottom-center joint to midpoint nodes on the left and right rafters.
A horizontal straining beam belongs to queen-post layouts, not the default king-post layout.
The CAD model shows geometry and connection intent only.
main_features: left and right angled struts from bottom center to rafter midpoint nodes
gusset plates at supports, apex, midpoint, and strut-to-rafter nodes
support pads at both bearing points
design_rules: Use two sloped rafters from supports to apex.
Split each rafter at the strut-to-rafter node: left support to left strut node, left strut node to apex, apex to right strut node, and right strut node to right support.
Add one vertical post from bottom midpoint to apex.
Add two angled struts from the bottom-center joint to midpoint nodes on the rafters.
Do not add a horizontal straining beam, collar beam, or crossbar between rafters unless explicitly requested.
Keep support, apex, center, and strut-to-rafter nodes connected with gussets.
validation_criteria: triangular roof outline with bottom chord
rafters are segmented through the left and right strut nodes
two diagonal struts rising from bottom center to the rafters
no horizontal member between the rafters
failure_modes: one long rafter hides or skips the strut-to-rafter joint
horizontal straining beam added to a default king-post truss
filled triangular plate instead of separate members

parts.name: Queen-post roof truss

queen_post_height.formula: rise / 2 for a simple symmetric visual model

assumptions: Symmetric roof truss with queen posts at quarter points.
The straining beam connects the tops of the queen posts.
Rafters pass through the queen-post top nodes and meet at the apex.
No diagonal internal braces are included unless the user explicitly asks for bracing.
OpenSCAD geometry is visual, not a structural certification.
main_features: rafter joints at the tops of the queen posts
gusset plates at supports, post feet, post tops, and apex
design_rules: Place queen posts symmetrically at +/- span/4.
Connect post tops with a horizontal straining beam.
Build rafters as four connected segments: left support to left post top, left post top to apex, apex to right post top, and right post top to right support.
Do not add diagonal internal braces, V braces, or floating members unless explicitly requested.
validation_criteria: rafters pass through both queen-post top nodes
no floating member above or away from the truss
no diagonal internal braces in the default queen-post layout
failure_modes: only one central post, which is a king-post truss
collapsed narrow truss instead of a wide span

parts.name: Pratt and Howe bridge truss family

main_parameters.depth: top chord to bottom chord spacing

assumptions: Verticals are included at panel points.
Pratt diagonals slope toward the span center in the usual gravity-load convention.
Howe diagonals slope away from the span center.
The generated OpenSCAD model is a layout model, not an analysis model.
main_features: gusset plates at all panel nodes
design_rules: Use Pratt when diagonals should slope toward center.
Use Howe when diagonals should slope away from center.
Keep panel_count even for symmetric center behavior.
validation_criteria: top chord and bottom chord are continuous
diagonals have the requested Pratt or Howe direction
failure_modes: diagonals reversed for the requested truss type

parts.name: Warren, Fink, and K-truss web patterns

main_parameters.depth: Warren or K-truss top-bottom chord spacing

non_main_parameters.mid_node_height: K-truss internal node height, usually depth/2

assumptions: Warren trusses use alternating triangular web members.
Fink trusses are pitched roof trusses with a W-shaped web layout.
K-trusses split panels into shorter diagonals meeting a mid-height node.
OpenSCAD output is a parametric geometry pattern, not a load rating.
main_features: Fink: pitched rafters with W-web below
K-truss: mid-height nodes and K-shaped web members
gusset plates at all major nodes
design_rules: Use Warren for alternating bridge triangles.
Use Fink for residential or light roof truss prompts.
Use K-truss for deep bridge or industrial frame prompts.
Do not substitute a solid zig-zag plate for individual members.
